origin.description: Fill ${expression} and $[format]{expression} from an environment or a list.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A template. A character vector is collapsed with an empty separator before scanning.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: Where the expressions are evaluated. A list supplies the names.

origin.details: Superseded by str_glue. A placeholder is ${expression} or $[format]{expression}. format is a sprintf specification. A lone dollar stays a dollar. A placeholder inside another placeholder is an error.
origin.example:
cat(str_interp(
  "One value, ${value1}, and then another, ${value2*2}.",
  list(value1 = 10, value2 = 20)
), "\n", sep = "")
cat(str_interp(
  "User ${user_name} (account $[08d]{account}) has $$[.2f]{amount}.",
  list(user_name = "smbache", account = 1337, amount = 6.656)
), "\n", sep = "")

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A template string, or a list of strings collapsed with an empty separator.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: A dict of names. Expressions are Python.

translation.details: The character vector is joined before scanning, and a missing piece makes that join missing. $[08d] and $[.2f] use the same sprintf codes. A doubled dollar leaves one dollar in front of a placeholder.
translation.value: A list of one interpolated string.
translation.example:
from stringr.interp import str_interp

print(str_interp(
    "One value, ${value1}, and then another, ${value2*2}.",
    {"value1": 10, "value2": 20},
)[0])
print(str_interp(
    "User ${user_name} (account $[08d]{account}) has $$[.2f]{amount}.",
    {"user_name": "smbache", "account": 1337, "amount": 6.656},
)[0])
